meta.face: A small, thin, clean-shaven old priest of about seventy with long snow-white hair falling to his collar, a high pale smooth forehead, a narrow gentle face, deep-set luminous eyes raised in prayer.
meta.basis: Eyewitness descriptions in Monnin's Life (Bishop Ullathorne, 1854: hair white as snow, eyes deep in shadow and preternaturally bright); he refused to be photographed, so Cabuchet's bust and the 1859 deathbed photograph fixed the type. The excerpt is from his catechism on prayer.

meta.face: An old man of about seventy, bald on the crown with a fringe of grey hair, a long grey beard narrowing to a point, a lean ascetic face, a steady upward gaze. The beard is grey and tapering, not broad and white.
meta.basis: The Painter's Manual (an old man with a broad beard) and the Hosios Loukas mosaic, kept grey and tapering to stay apart from the white-bearded elders; the lions from his martyrdom. The excerpt is his memorial's communion antiphon, from his Letter to the Romans.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Ignatius of Antioch (Hosios Loukas mosaic)
Didron, Manuel d'iconographie chrétienne (Dionysius of Fourna)

meta.face: A young noblewoman of about twenty with long fair golden hair under a red veil, a serene oval face, large dark eyes and a composed, steadfast expression.

meta.face: Perpetua: about twenty-two, dark hair bound up under a white veil, a composed oval face and a direct, fearless gaze. Felicity: slightly younger, a simpler rounder face, dark hair under a plain veil, a gentle lowered gaze.
meta.basis: The Passion of Perpetua and Felicity (Perpetua about twenty-two, noble, a nursing mother; Felicity a slave who gave birth in prison; the ladder of Perpetua's vision) and the Ravenna mosaics, which dress Felicity more plainly. Their colouring is not attested. The excerpt is Perpetua's answer to the procurator.

sources.title: The Passion of Perpetua and Felicity (New Advent)
